text:
Ethan: Heads-up 1: ACME wants final presales numbers for their POC: committed baseline + burst plan + preheat cost. They also returned the security questionnaire.
Priya: Quick summary from ACME SRE: steady 180 QPS (chat sends), 25% diurnal spike to 480 QPS, median seq ~100 tokens, 99th ~350. They want <200ms p95 latency.
Ethan: They prefer reserved GPUs for predictable p95. Procurement asked: how many reserved slots and what's the burst charging model?
Diego: For latency target and those qps, start with 5 reserved high-throughput slots (A10/NVIDIA-equivalent). With batching and KV cache that covers ~200-250 steady QPS. Autoscale up to 11 to hit 480 QPS headroom.
Nina: What's our recommended preheat strategy for KV/prefix warm? They said many repeat prefixes but 6k uniques daily, top 1.5k are hot.
Diego: Run a two-phase preheat: (1) top-1.5k prefixes during a 60m targeted prewarm, (2) progressive background cold-fill for tail over 12h. Expect ~3-7% additional token cost during preheat.
Ethan: Procurement wants a single-line "preheat fee" for the SOW. Any sample wording and numbers?
Priya: Sample: "One-time preheat: 5 reserved slots x 1.0 hour x hourly-rate = est. $X (billed actuals if exceeded)." Add note: synthetic/scrubbed data only.
Nina: Security flags: ACME requires BYOK for KMS, 12-month audit log retention, and proof that model weights are ephemeral. We can meet BYOK on Enterprise/Private.
Diego: Also add fallback model plan in case of saturation: primary full model on reserved pool -> fallback quantized variant on same pool -> degrade-to-short-context model on spot capacity. We'll configure gradational quality degrade + rate-limit.
Ethan: Can someone paste a compact autoscale policy snippet we can include?
Diego: Paste:
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 5
  max_replicas: 11
  target_qps_per_replica: 40
  burst_buffer_tokens: 350
  cooldown_seconds: 45
  prewarm:
    duration: 60m
    prefixes_runbook: preheat-hot-prefixes.sh
```
Priya: Note: target_qps_per_replica tuned conservative to hit p95 SLAs. We should mention CPU/IO headroom for batching.
Ethan: Data residency: ACME wants EU-only POC. Can we provision reserved pool in eu-west-1 and run preheat there? Lead time?
capacity-bot: `rbctl reservations create --region eu-west-1 --type reserved --count 5` -> estimated provisioning lead: 3 business days; 2 pre-provisioned slots currently available in vendor pool.
Diego: We'll open infra ticket. For Dedicated theres no cross-region routing, so EU pool is fine. There may be a small premium for regional reserved capacity.
Nina: Security note for SOW: preheat exercises must use synthetic or hashed payloads; include a clause that we won't persist PII.
Ethan: Procurement also asked how burst billing is invoiced if they exceed reserved capacity.
Priya: Billing guidance: reserved covers baseline throughput. Burst uses either (A) reserved burst credits included up to X hours/month (we suggest 10% buffer) or (B) on-demand overage billed per-minute at on-demand rate. Suggest we show both options in quote.
Diego: Suggest adding a "burst credit" line item equal to estimated 12% of monthly reserved cost for POC to reduce on-demand surprises.
Ethan: Any SLA/rollback concerns if autoscale fails during spike? We need a clear failure-mode note.
Diego: Add runbook: (1) auto-fallback to quantized model, (2) route non-critical traffic to lower-cost region or spot. Also offer an assisted-ops play: we run first-day watch for 8 hours as part of onboarding (add to SOW).
Nina: ACME asked for SOC/ISO artifacts. I have the package ready; will attach when drafting SOW.
Ethan: Next steps: Priya will draft cost lines + burst option. Diego will open infra provisioning ticket and attach autoscale snippet. Nina will prepare security SOW clause and attach compliance docs. I'll consolidate and send to ACME.
Priya: I'll DM the rough numbers for review before sending.
Ethan: Thanks team. Closing thread; will re-open if ACME pushes back on numbers. :white_check_mark:
